To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AAF-induced liver injury results in the proliferation of biliary stem cells and that this proliferation is regulated by glucocorticoids.

oval cell proliferation is stimulated by AAF-induced hepatocyte injury and that AAF-induced proliferation of oval cells is initiated by the proliferation of the terminal ductular structures that are the primary niche for hepatic stem cells.
AAF-induced liver carcinogenesis involves the proliferation of the terminal hepatic biliary epithelial ductules that constitute the hepatic stem cell compartment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the origin and the mechanism(s) of oval cell proliferation.
the origin, proliferation and differentiation of the early proliferated oval cells and their role in regeneration and carcinogenesis.
the identification and characterization of a hepatic stem cell population and the elucidation of its potential role in the liver regeneration process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oval cells are a population of bipotent progenitor cells, which are capable of differentiation into hepatocytes and biliary epithelial cell lineages.
the oval cell compartment of the liver is not homogeneous and consists of different subpopulations with varying differentiation potentials.
AAF-induced proliferation of biliary ductules is the origin of oval cell proliferation in rat liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oval cells are derived from the biliary epithelial cell lineage and that they are the progeny of a population of cells that have the ability to differentiate into hepatocyte, biliary, pancreatic and intestinal cell types.
the oval cells are the progenitor cells of the liver, and that they are generated by proliferation of biliary stem cells.
the oval cells are a heterogeneous population of progenitor cells with the capacity of differentiation into several cell types, including hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early proliferating biliary epithelial oval cells represent a unique cell population that is distinct from the hepatocytes and bile epithelial cells in terms of both origin and function.

the early proliferating cells in the AAF model of liver injury are not the same as the oval cells in the bile ligation model, and that oval cells are a heterogeneous group of cells with different developmental potential and lineage relationships.
the oval cell response in rat liver after AAF administration is a consequence of the proliferation of the terminal bile ductules that are the primary stem cell niche in the liver.
